statement: We do not know whether Theorem 3 holds for all classes of (bounded-arity) relational structures.
context: 5 Conclusions We do not know whether Theorem 3 holds for all classes of (bounded-arity) relational structures. With more technicalities (but the same ideas as presented in this extended abstract), one can weaken the assumption on a fan class to obtain the same result (Theorem 3). In particular, it suffices to require that there are polynomials f1 , f2 , f3 , f4 such that for any parameters k, r, `1 , `2 ∈ N, G(C) contains the fan-grid L(k 0 , r0 , `01 , `02 ), where k 0 = f1 (k, r, `1 , `2 ) ≥ k, r0 = f2 (k, r, `1 , `2 ) ≥ r, `01 = f3 (k, r, `1 , `2 ) ≥ `1 , `02 = f4 (k, r, `1 , `2 ) ≥ `2 . This can be achieved by making use of Lemma 9 (as it would not be possible to test directly for cliques of all sizes) and by a modification of the construction from Section 4.1 (to accommodate for the fact that some fan-grids may not correspond to cliques due to incompatible numbers).
